newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Holiday firm Airtours sees busy summer.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Holiday firm Airtours sees busy summer.

text.p: Shares in Airtours Plc reported strong gains on Wednesday after the British holiday company forecast a bright outlook for the summer.
Chairman and chief executive David Crossland described the six months to end-March as "very satisfactory" after seasonal losses shrank by 45 percent to 12.7 million pounds ($20.7 million).

"With booking levels and load factors in our major markets showing appreciable gains over the previous year we look forward with confidence to the second half of the year," Crossland said in a statement.
Airtours usually posts a loss in the first half of the year before swinging into profit on the strength of its performance in the high season.
The market welcomed the figures and sunny prospects, and Airtours shares gained 27 pence to 971.5p by 1000 GMT.

The holiday company, in which Miami-based cruise tour operator Carnival Corp has a stake of almost 30 percent, said it had seen significant improvements in Britain and Scandinavia -- its two largest markets.

Turnover climbed by 34 percent to 818 million pounds and Airtours lifted the interim dividend by 23 percent to four pence per share. Overseas operations now account for more than half the company's revenues.
Airtours sells holidays in Canada and has recently launched a new tour operator based in California.

"The first part of our strategy was to build a second stream of earnings to equal the UK," Crossland told Reuters. "Now we'd quite like three equal streams of revenue - the UK, Scandinavia and the rest of the world."
Britain accounted for some 375 million pounds of first half turnover, Scandinavia 340 million and North America just over 100 million.

Crossland said Airtours had spent 250 million on acquisitions over the past six years and seen profits leap from just six million to 86 million last year. The company has another 250 million pounds to spend.

Airtours, which carries some five million passengers annually, has already launched its 1998 summer holiday brochures in the UK -- before most people have jetted off to soak up the sun on this year's package.
Crossland said the move enabled the company to persuade people to book again for next year in the "two week afterglow" of a happy holiday.
Brochures are also available in resorts to allow holidaymakers to inspect other hotels where they might want to stay next year.
Airtours and its rival Thomson Travel Corp are the subject of a UK Monopolies and Mergers Commission (MMC) probe into ownership links between tour operators and travel agency chains.
Both companies have extensive networks of British high street travel agents.
Crossland said he felt the inquiry would clear the air and prove that Britons were getting a good deal.
"We are in a very competitive market and the consumer in the UK gets the best value in the world for his holiday," he said. ($ = 0.613 British Pounds)
